text:
mira: Heads up — after the 1.28 cluster roll in eu-west-1 I'm seeing GPU nodegroups flapping and CA removing entire node pools. Pods with gpu resource keep pending. Anyone else?

aj: yup saw it too. Looks like providerID format changed for the managed nodegroup nodes, autoscaler can't match nodes to ASG/nodegroup.

leo: logs from CA show: 
```
I1124 12:03:22.123456 123 autoscaler.go:456] Node not found for providerID: aws:///eu-west-1a/i-0abcd... skipping
```

mira: exact. The cloud provider plugin now reports providerID with region prefix (was short) so the nodegroup lookup fails. This only affects GPU nodepools because we use a custom label -> nodegroup mapping for gpupools.

emma: consequence = CA thinks nodes are gone and scales up replacements in a different nodegroup, then deletes old ones. Costs + pods stuck because the new nodes don't get GPU drivers for a short window.

aj: reproducer: upgraded a staging cluster to k8s 1.28 and ran a bunch of cuda pods, CA removed the nodegroup owning the pods.

mira: short-term mitigation: pin cluster-autoscaler image to v1.25-legacy which uses the old providerID parsing. We're doing that now on staging.

leo: long term we need autoscaler patch to normalize providerID formats and fallback to node labels when providerID lookup fails. I started a PR draft: https://github.com/redwood/autoscaler/pull/xyz (WIP).

infra-bot: deploy started: pinned cluster-autoscaler -> redwood/cluster-autoscaler:v1.25-legacy in staging (deployment/cluster-autoscaler).

oncall: any immediate customer impact?

emma: a few low-traffic customer jobs delayed ~15-30m in eu-west-1, some cost spike from replacement nodes, but no SLA breaches yet.

aj: perf note — the fallback to label mapping will need to be careful: gpupool labeling varies across nodepool templates in prod. We should avoid global heuristics. Suggest mapping config per nodepool poolID -> label set.

mira: agreed. For now rolling hotfix to control plane: patch autoscaler to try providerID parsing variants (old/new) and then fallback to matching `node.kubernetes.io/instance-type` + `redwood/gpupool` label. Small patch is under review.

leo: here's the quick patch snippet I used in staging: 
```
// try old providerID style
if !match(providerID) {
   providerID = normalizeProviderID(providerID)
}
// fallback to labels
if nodeLookupFail {
   tryLookupByLabels(node.Labels["redwood/gpupool"], node.Labels["node.kubernetes.io/instance-type"])
}
```

mira: timeline — if staging looks good we'll push the CA normalization hotfix to eu-west-1 prod tonight during the 22:00 maintenance window.

oncall: monitoring: adding grafana alert for nodegroup deletion rate + pending GPU pods.

emma: also filing a ticket to review node template generation in our provisioning repo — we accidentally changed label conventions between 2024-10 and 2025-01 templates which made mapping brittle.

aj: FYI this also affects spot/preemptible pools where providerID differences combine with instances terminating. ⚠️

leo: will follow up with PR and a unit test matrix for providerID formats across cloud regions.

mira: thanks — will post rollout plan and rollback steps after staging validation. If anyone sees more pending gpu pods ping @oncall and I'll re-open the hotfix. :thumbsup:
